title: Upgrade attention kernels: FlashAttentionV2 + fused ops, rope/rotary, KV-batching and scheduler tweaks
author: Samantha Li
description: Motivation: Improve throughput and tail latency for medium-long sequence workloads by upgrading our attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2, adding fused rotary/rope ops, and ensuring compatibility with continuous KV caching and our scheduler's batching heuristics. This PR introduces kernel upgrades, operator fusion for Rope/Rotary + softmax, KV-batching integration to reduce redundant key/value materialization, and multiple scheduler micro-optimizations to better pack tokens across streams. Benchmarks: internal perf runs on A100 80GB show up to 1.6x throughput for seq_len=2048 and 20-30% median latency reduction across a mix of chat and instruction workloads. Changes are conservative and feature-flag gated to allow staged rollout. Checklist: - [x] Integrate FlashAttentionV2 kernels with our op registry - [x] Implement fused rope/rotary CUDA kernels and CPU fallback - [x] KV-cache changes to support batched KV materialization and reuse - [x] Scheduler changes to improve packing across short-lived streams - [x] Add unit + perf tests and backfill CI benchmarks - [x] Docs and rollout notes - [x] Canary rollout to Dedicated clusters Notes: The description below includes a short summary of commits, files changed, reviewers' comments and CI history. The body of this PR is intentionally a single continuous string to match export format.
commits: feat(attn): add FlashAttentionV2 wrapper and selection logic
perf(attn): fused rope/rotary CUDA kernel with scaled softmax
feat(kv): KV-batching materialization path for shared KV references
refactor(scheduler): packing heuristic to prioritize long-running streams
test(perf): add end-to-end perf harness for FlashAttnV2 path
docs: perf notes and rollout instructions
review_comments: Marco Alvarez: Nice work—can you call out the compatibility matrix for supported CUDA/cuBLAS versions? We should gate on >=11.8 and nvcc 12.1 to avoid subtle FP differences.
Samantha Li: Added a runtime capability check and fallback to the existing FlashAttentionV1 path. Updated docs to call out CUDA >=11.8, driver >=525.90.
Jade Thompson: I saw a perf regression on seq_len=128 microbench on CPU fallback. Can we add a special-casing to keep old slow path for tiny sequences?
Samantha Li: Added an override: seq_len<256 uses existing baseline kernels on CPU. Documented in comments and unit tests added.

Daniel Park: KV-batching change looks good but add a safety net so we don't accidentally reuse KV state across customer sessions. Suggest adding an explicit session-scoped cache key and an assert in debug builds.
Samantha Li: Implemented session-scoped cache key and debug-time validation. Also added an integration test that simulates two concurrent sessions.
Marco Alvarez: CI failed initially on lint and a numeric edge-case in softmax for large negative logits. After the fix CI is green. Approving.
Jade Thompson: Ran canary on one Dedicated pool overnight; tail latencies improved and error budget unaffected. Approving.
ci_checks: perf_regression_checks: passed (no regressions on baseline workloads)
merge_outcome: Merged to main after approvals and successful canary
release_notes: Performance: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rope/rotary ops and KV-batching support. Expect up to 1.6x throughput on long sequences and improved median and tail latency. Rollout: feature-flagged and will be enabled by default after canary.
notes_for_ops: Enable via runtime flag attn.flashattn_v2.enabled=true. For Dedicated/Private deployments ensure CUDA>=11.8 and drivers >=525.90. Monitor attn.flashattn_v2.errors and kv.batching.hit_rate dashboards during rollout.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: numerical differences and edge-case regressions on tiny sequences. Mitigation: CPU fallback for seq_len<256, runtime cap check and feature flag, debug-time KV cache validation, staged canary rollout.
testing_summary: Added unit tests for fused kernel correctness, end-to-end perf harness, integration tests for KV-batching semantics, and a canary run against a Dedicated pool. All tests green in CI after fixes.
